problems.title: A decreasing logarithm reverses the inequality
problems.question: Solve $\log_{1/2}(x^2+2x)<\log_{1/2}(x+6)$.
problems.idea: Keep both arguments positive before comparing them.
steps: The domain is x>-6 together with x<-2 or x>0.
Compare arguments: x²+2x>x+6 gives (x+3)(x-2)>0, so x<-3 or x>2.

problems.title: Read the entire radical in a logarithm base
problems.question: Find the domain of $\log_{\sqrt{x-3}}[\sqrt{10-2x}/(x-4)]$.
problems.idea: Check base validity and strict argument positivity.
steps: The base √(x-3) requires x>3 and x≠4.
The numerator must be strictly positive, giving x<5. Since the numerator is positive, the denominator must also be positive, giving x>4.
problems.note: In the original PDF the radical in the base covers x-3. Reading it as √x-3 would describe a different function.

problems.title: A familiar small-angle ratio
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to0}3\tan(2x)/[2\sin(3x)]$.
problems.idea: Extract the linear angle factors.

problems.title: A standard-position hyperbola from eccentricity
problems.question: A hyperbola passes through (-5,3) and has eccentricity √2. Find its standard-position equation.
problems.idea: Use the centre and axis alignment implicit in the answer choices.
problems.note: Passing through one point and knowing eccentricity does not determine a completely arbitrary translated or rotated hyperbola. The listed choices implicitly fix the centre at the origin and axes along the coordinate axes.

problems.title: A downward-opening parabola
problems.question: Find the parabola symmetric about the y-axis and passing through (0,0) and (6,-2).
problems.idea: Its vertex at the origin makes the equation y=kx².
formulas: A y-axis-symmetric parabola through the origin has equation y=kx².

problems.title: Compare leading powers in a sequence limit
problems.question: Find $\lim_{n\to\infty}(3+6+\cdots+3n)/\sqrt{2n^4+5n^2+2}$.
problems.idea: Sum the numerator and divide by n².
steps: After division by n² the ratio is (3/2)(1+1/n)/√(2+5/n²+2/n⁴).

problems.title: A conjugate creates the cancelling factor
problems.question: Find $\lim_{x\to2}\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x+x^2}-\sqrt{7+2x-x^2}}{x^2-2x}$.
problems.idea: Rationalize the root difference.
steps: After multiplying by the conjugate, cancel x-2.

problems.title: Simplify before differentiating
problems.question: Differentiate $(\sin(x/2)-\cos(x/2))^2$.
problems.idea: Expand using the double-angle identity.

problems.title: An even differentiable function has zero slope at zero
problems.question: Find $y\prime(0)$ for $y=\sqrt{(4-x^2)/(4+x^2)}$.
problems.idea: Differentiate the inner even quotient.
formulas: If u=(4-x²)/(4+x²), then u′=-16x/(4+x²)² and y′=u′/(2√u).
steps: Near zero the radicand is positive, so the derivative exists.
At zero, u=1 and u′=0, yielding y′(0)=0.

problems.title: Increasing branch of a radical quadratic
problems.question: Find the intervals of increase of $y=\sqrt{x^2-5x+6}$.
problems.idea: Use its disconnected domain and derivative sign.
formulas: Domain x≤2 or x≥3; y′=(2x-5)/(2√(x²-5x+6)) in the interiors.
steps: On x<2 the numerator is negative, so the function decreases.
On x>3 the numerator is positive, so it increases.
Including the continuous domain endpoint, the maximal increasing branch is [3,∞).
problems.note: The printed choice (3,∞) gives the usual open derivative-sign interval. Its smaller subintervals are also increasing, but do not give the full branch.

problems.title: Maximum on a positive logarithm interval
problems.question: Find the maximum of y=x³lnx for 1≤x≤e.
problems.idea: The derivative has a fixed sign.
steps: The maximum is at x=e, with y=e³·1=e³.

problems.title: Give both curvature signs
problems.question: Find the curvature intervals of y=x⁶-6x⁵+7.5x⁴+3x.
problems.idea: Factor the second derivative.
steps: For x<1, y″≥0, with an isolated zero at x=0; the graph is concave up throughout (-∞,1).
For 1<x<3, y″<0, so the graph is concave down.
For x>3, y″>0, so it is concave up. The sign does not change at 0.
problems.note: The source’s translated curvature term can be read in opposite conventions. The second-derivative signs specify precisely which intervals apply.

problems.title: An inflection point with an incorrect printed coordinate
problems.question: Find the inflection point of y=xeˣ.
problems.idea: The second derivative must change sign.
steps: Since eˣ>0, the second derivative changes from negative to positive at x=-2.
problems.note: The nearest printed choice gives (-2,-e⁻²), missing the factor 2. None of the choices gives the exact point.

problems.title: Polynomial division finds the slant asymptote
problems.question: Find the slant asymptote of $(x^3-2x^2+2)/(2x^2-x)$.
problems.idea: The degree-one quotient is the asymptote.
steps: The remaining rational term (2-3x/4)/(2x²-x) tends to zero at either infinity.

problems.title: A half-angle identity makes an integral standard
problems.question: Find $\int dx/(1+\cos2x)$.
problems.idea: Replace the denominator with twice a cosine square.
steps: Thus an antiderivative is (1/2)tanx+C on each domain interval.

problems.title: Integrate negative powers
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_1^4(1+\sqrt x)/x^2\,dx$.
problems.idea: Split the integrand into two powers.
steps: The integrand is x⁻²+x^(-3/2), with antiderivative -1/x-2/√x.
Its value at 4 is -5/4 and at 1 is -3.

problems.title: Triangular prism from a circumradius
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has height 8 cm and base circumradius 2 cm. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Its base is equilateral.
steps: The base side is 2√3 and its area is 3√3.

problems.title: Area between two sideways parabolas
problems.question: Find the area enclosed by 3y=x² and 3x=y².
problems.idea: Find the intersections and integrate top minus bottom.
steps: Substitute y=x²/3 into y²=3x to get x⁴=27x, giving intersections (0,0),(3,3).
For 0≤x≤3, the upper curve is y=√(3x), lower y=x²/3.

problems.title: A disk-method volume
problems.question: Rotate the region under $y=1/\cos x$ for $0\le x\le\pi/4$ about the x-axis. Find V/π.
problems.idea: The cross-section is a disk of radius secx.

problems.title: Distance from the origin to a plane
problems.question: Find the distance from the origin to 2x+3y-4z-1=0.
problems.idea: Use the normal length.
steps: At the origin the numerator is |-1|=1.

problems.title: Largest rectangle in an equilateral triangle
problems.question: A rectangle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side 1 with one side on the base. Find its largest area.
problems.idea: The available width decreases linearly with height.
formulas: Triangle height H=√3/2; rectangle width=1-h/H; A=h(1-h/H).
steps: The maximum is H/4 at h=H/2 and width 1/2.

problems.title: Dihedral angle of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has all edges equal. Find the sine of the dihedral angle at a lateral edge.
problems.idea: Take a cross-section perpendicular to that edge.
formulas: For a regular tetrahedron, cosδ=1/3; sin²δ+cos²δ=1.
steps: Let the common edge be AB and its midpoint M. For other vertices C,D, MC=MD=√3a/2 while CD=a.
The angle CMD is the internal dihedral angle. The cosine rule gives cosδ=[2(3a²/4)-a²]/[2(3a²/4)]=1/3.

problems.title: Separate a rational integrand
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_1^2(x^2+3x+5)/x\,dx$.
problems.idea: Divide each numerator term by x.
steps: At 2 the antiderivative is 8+5ln2. At 1 it is 7/2.

problems.title: The volume choices omit π
problems.question: Find the volume under $y=\sqrt x$, $1\le x\le\sqrt2$, rotated about the x-axis.
problems.idea: Square the radius in the disk formula.
problems.note: The printed choices contain no factor π. The choice 1/2 would give V/π, but the question asks for V. Rotating only a curve makes a surface; volume uses the region beneath it as conventionally intended.

problems.title: Area between a square and cube root
problems.question: Find the area enclosed by y=x² and y=∛x.
problems.idea: Only nonnegative intersection x-values are possible.
steps: The equations meet at x=0,1. For x<0 the cube root is negative while x²≥0, so there are no negative intersections.
On (0,1), the cube root is above the square.
